races.name: AJA Novice Flat Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes (For Riders With 3 Wins Or Fewer At Start Of Season)

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: Despite her name she is a hold-up type in recent form, with three thirds over 2m on good ground and modest finishing effort; Sam England's yard is 1/4 in the last 14 days and the 48-day break is worth noting, but her best form has come at 16f+ rather than this 1m4f trip.|

runners_data.name: Cougar
runners_data.note: Michael Chapman's seven-year-old has two wins on soft ground and none on good in recent history (0W0P on good in 15 runs), so the going is a significant question; genuinely suited to hold-up racing but pushed into a midfield role by the composition of this field, which limits his chance of getting a natural run.|

runners_data.name: Palazzo Persico
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll has been notably active (3/42 in 14 days) and this five-year-old's only win came on soft over 10f — stepping up to 1m4f on good turf is a genuine query; however, the sprint-finish scenario plays to his quick-fire style, and he drops into a weak race off OR 59.|

runners_data.name: He's Our Cracker
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish is in good form (4/21) and this four-year-old is a true hold-up type whose natural race position is at the rear, placed in midfield here only because the entire field is rear-facing; his form figures on good going are thin (3/10) and his recent proximity figures at 1m3f-1m4f are mixed.|

runners_data.name: Ruler Of The River
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's six-year-old carries a tongue-tie and has been absent 63 days; his last five runs are mostly at 2m+ on soft, and while he has a placing over 2m on good, dropping back to 1m4f on good turf is a significant stylistic and conditions stretch — his true profile is a stayer who wants cut.|

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Gary Rutherford's five-year-old has consistent form on good going (6 placings from 11 runs, 0W) and has been placed over 9f-12f at recent starts; 15 days since last run keeps him fresh, and his repeated placings suggest a reliable finisher who may prove competitive if the sprint finish produces a clean run.|

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners carrying a hold-up profile and no genuine front-runner in the field, this 1m4f Catterick contest is almost certain to be run at a crawling early tempo, with the field bunched and waiting before a sprint-style finish erupts in the straight. Made All, despite her name, is rated a hold-up type on her recent profile, and Palazzo Persico has no obvious motivation to go forward either, meaning the race will likely drift along in a slow-motion convoy until jockeys begin to commit turning for home. The field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Cougar, He's Our Cracker, Ruler Of The River, and On The Bubble are all true hold-up types repositioned to midfield, but in practice several of them will be sitting last or second-last with nowhere to go in a truly slowly-run race. The race shape overwhelmingly favours the horse that can produce the sharpest late burst from a good position — ideally one who gets a prominent or handy berth by accident of a slow pace rather than design, and who has the best turn-of-foot for a flat-out sprint finish on good turf.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow pace, sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles through the early stages and the race becomes a late dash up Catterick's straight, positioning in the final two furlongs is everything.
scenarios.body: With no horse committed to setting fractions, the pace will be modest and the race compressed into a furlong-and-a-half sprint; those who can secure a handy berth mid-race without getting shuffled back will have the decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy mover capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If one runner manages to land a prominent position from an early slow burn and sustains it into the straight before rivals find their stride.
scenarios.body: In a bunch finish where the gaps are tight, the horse that travels widest or finds the clearest daylight on the turn will get first run on tired rivals; Palazzo Persico's win record on cut-back surfaces and On The Bubble's course-going form suit this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly less crawling than expected and genuine hold-up horses get a true staying test over the 1m4f trip.
scenarios.body: Ruler Of The River has a staying profile and any increase in tempo would suit his genuine hold-up style; Cougar has won on soft and while good going is an unknown, any honest pace that stretches the field exposes his latent ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and interference
scenarios.trigger: If the sprint-finish becomes a messy multi-horse scramble with interference, jostling for room, or a late challenge from an unexpected rival.
scenarios.body: Amateur jockeys navigating a tight Catterick finish in a truly slowly-run race create significant risk of positional errors and wide draws being decisive; He's Our Cracker or Made All could benefit if rivals check or are hampered.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a near-stationary early gallop — with six hold-up types and no confirmed front-runner, the pace in the first mile could be dangerously slow, making positional decisions by the amateur jockeys on the turn far more decisive than form.|

Palazzo Persico's step up to 1m4f on good turf is unproven — his only win came on soft at 10f and if the good ground and extra distance expose a stamina limit, his chance evaporates in the straight despite looking sharp in a slow-run dash.|

Ruler Of The River is 63 days off the track and his last five starts are exclusively at 2m+ on soft or heavy — the combination of distance drop, good turf, and layoff makes him a significant watch for signs of flat-footedness in a race he looks ill-suited to.|

Monitor how many of the redistributed hold-up types (Cougar, He's Our Cracker, On The Bubble, Ruler Of The River) end up genuinely at the rear — if four horses are bunched last, the sprint finish will be a lottery of who finds daylight first rather than who is most talented.|

Amateur jockey claims and inexperience (three riders on 3-win or fewer claim) combined with a slow gallop at Catterick's tight turns create elevated risk of traffic problems on the bend — horses with wide draws or jockeys who commit early could steal a march.|

races.name: EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lion Of Persia
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with two runs on good ground (finished 4th and 8th over 5f), so the trip and surface are familiar; Robert Cowell is a sharp sprint handler and Marco Ghiani is in form, but this runner needs to be ridden more prominently than usual to benefit from the likely race shape — the race tempo and flat track may suit if sent forward early.

runners_data.name: Longshanks Luke
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Patrick Neville with no form lines to read, making style and fitness entirely unknown; Paul Mulrennan is a canny northern jockey who will likely attempt to secure a pitch close to the pace, and if this horse has ability it arrives in the right race for a forward-travelling type — a significant unknown that could be anything.

runners_data.name: Neverbeatdeswalker
runners_data.note: One run to his name (7th over 6f on good) so stepping down to 5f is a query, and Mark Walford's runners rarely blaze out of nowhere; a genuine hold-up type who will need the pace to cut back dramatically to be involved, which this race shape is unlikely to deliver.

runners_data.name: Johns Power
runners_data.note: Showed little in two starts (6th and 10th), and while Joanna Mason is a tidy rider, this horse's natural rearward style is squeezed further by the volume of hold-up rivals — running out of its preferred role in midfield mapping makes its already modest form look harder to translate into a result.

runners_data.name: Kaiulani Spirit
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends this one out 20 days after its latest run having placed form on good and soft ground, suggesting solid ground suitability; a true hold-up runner bumped into midfield by the cluster of closers in this field, its STYLE_FIT of 0.90 is a real concern on a flat 5f where getting the natural position matters.

runners_data.name: Mick's The Boy
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — a confirmed prominent runner who finished 2nd over 6f and is stepping down to 5f where he can press on from the gate; Michael & David Easterby have had three winners from 30 runners in the last 14 days, and with Lewis Chalkley on board and no one to challenge his lead, controlling the race from the front is entirely achievable.

runners_data.name: Mr De Maggs
runners_data.note: One run, finished last of ten over 6f on good, and carries a fades-in-finish flag that is a serious concern in a race where the hold-up brigade will already be scrambling for the same late ground; Zak Wheatley on board and a trainer with only four runners in the last fortnight — hard to make a case.

runners_data.name: South West
runners_data.note: Drops from OR 67 in a Band C/D race showing glimpses (3rd and 5th from five starts), and Daniel Tudhope is a strong tactical jockey who will look to improve its position; wears a hood, is 11 days since last run, and has genuine good-ground form over 5f — but its natural hold-up style is displaced into midfield here, which the horse must overcome to deliver.

runners_data.name: Prosperity Angel
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Ben Haslam with no known form, another complete unknown in terms of style; Andrew Mullen is a capable northern rider and Haslam occasionally produces first-time-out novices ready to run — the lack of any information cuts both ways.

runners_data.name: Cheeky Chesca
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (2nd twice, 3rd once from six starts) with solid good-ground profile and wears a hood; Tim Easterby runner who wants to come from behind, but with four other true hold-up types competing for the same ground, finding daylight in this congested rear-group is the central challenge — the form is honest but the tactical conditions are against her.

races.paceDynamic: Mick's The Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner novice sprint and, with no other confirmed lead horse to push him, Lewis Chalkley can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish over Catterick's flat 5f. The field is loaded with hold-up horses — Johns Power, Kaiulani Spirit, South West, Cheeky Chesca, Lion Of Persia, Neverbeatdeswalker and Mr De Maggs all want to come from behind — meaning the closers will be tripping over each other for the same ground late, which blunts their collective effectiveness. Mick's The Boy sets a rhythm that suits a horse travelling prominently just off him rather than a horse needing a wall of pace to run into. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Johns Power, Kaiulani Spirit, South West and Cheeky Chesca are all genuine hold-up runners forced into a midfield mapping — the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent pitch behind Mick's The Boy are those with the tactical speed to push forward early, namely any of the two unknown-style runners (Longshanks Luke, Prosperity Angel) or Lion Of Persia if ridden more aggressively than form suggests. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can sit in behind an uncontested leader and pick up off a genuine but unforced gallop — true hold-up horses will struggle to find daylight through a congested pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mick's Boy Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy bowls along uncontested and sets a fair, even gallop that rewards horses racing in close attendance.
scenarios.body: Mick's The Boy dictates from the front and any horse with the tactical speed to sit second or third will have first run on the group; the closers, packed together and lacking a strong pace to aim at, will find traffic and arrive too late on a flat track with limited room to manoeuvre.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Unknown Debutant Lands
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two debutants (Longshanks Luke or Prosperity Angel) is well-prepared and trained for a prominent pitch, showing a natural racing style that slots in behind the leader.
scenarios.body: A lightly-raced or debut horse from a sharp yard can travel smoothly in the slipstream of the pace-setter without the form-book baggage of the hold-up horses; on a flat, straight 5f where there is little room for positional recovery, a debut runner with natural speed can punch through before rivals have gathered.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Picks Through
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy sets a genuinely strong gallop that strings the field out and creates a clear run for one hold-up horse that manages to find daylight on the outside.
scenarios.body: A true closer can only profit here if the pace is hot enough to unwind the leader and if that runner secures a clean outside passage — with so many rivals in the same style-band, the more likely outcome is a traffic-clogged finish, but the one horse who threads through first reaps the reward.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy goes off too fast, ties up in the final furlong, and a prominent pursuer sweeps past a field that has spread wide.
scenarios.body: An overly aggressive early pace on a flat, tight Catterick 5f can see the leader empty quickly, handing the race to whichever horse is travelling smoothly just off the pace at the two-furlong pole; this scenario requires a genuine misjudgement from Chalkley, which is possible but unlikely given the absence of any rival to pressure him.

watchPoints.text: Mick's The Boy — if Lewis Chalkley elects to go very hard early without any rival pressuring him, he risks overcooking a solo lead and handing the race to the nearest pursuer; the tempo he sets in the opening furlong dictates every scenario in this race.

South West and Cheeky Chesca — both are genuine hold-up horses wearing headgear, trained by yards with strong recent records, and both will likely be angled wide by Tudhope and Allan to find clear air; if they find the same gap at the same moment the risk of interference is real.

Longshanks Luke and Prosperity Angel — two debut runners whose unknown styles could scramble the early pace picture if either bolts forward or dwells badly; a debutant who fires up and chases Mick's The Boy uninvited would fundamentally change the pace dynamic.

Johns Power and Kaiulani Spirit — both are tagged as running out of role in the midfield, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 each, watch whether their jockeys (Mason and Fentiman) attempt to push forward from the gate early; if they do, it tightens the race for the one legitimate front-runner and disrupts the predicted settled scenario.

races.name: racingtv.com/freetrial Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lady Dublin
runners_data.note: Ran three times at 5f-7f on good and soft ground with a best effort of third at 7f; Harry Russell takes the ride for Ollie Pears who has had no winners in the last 14 days from four runners; the step up to 6f at Catterick is an unknown quantity but good-ground form is solid enough, and this runner's undefined style may see her pushed forward by default in a small field.
runners_data.comment: Lady Dublin has been freely competitive without adding a win, placing third and fourth in three of her last four starts and returning quickly 23 days on. Already race-tested over today's trip, she tops our figures at 70 and rates the one to beat on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Mardy Bum
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's yard is in decent form with two winners from 51 over 14 days, and Mark Winn is a competent pilot in northern nurseries; runs on a short turnaround of seven days and showed a placed effort in similar going, suggesting freshness is managed; though listed as hold-up, the small field may see this horse pushed into a more prominent position than it naturally seeks.
runners_data.comment: Mardy Bum has been competitive without breaking through, third and fourth in two of her last four starts, and returns quickly a week on. She rates 63 on our figures having raced over today's distance before, though the yard is currently out of form at 2 from 51 in a fortnight.

runners_data.name: Sunrise At Dawn
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster sends this runner back out after 30 days and it has not yet troubled the judge in three starts, finishing no better than fifth; Tom Eaves is an experienced northern jockey who will try to produce the horse late, but its two attempts on good ground have returned sixth and eighth, raising genuine concerns about its ability to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Sunrise At Dawn has yet to trouble the judge this campaign (6th, 8th, 5th) but rates comfortably above her official mark of 57 on our figures, up to 64, and has raced over today's distance before. A month since her last run, sharpness is the query.

runners_data.name: Showmethebubbles
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison has two winners from 12 in the past fortnight, and Cam Hardie rides a horse returning from 50 days off; in truth this is a genuine rear-of-field operator whose natural instinct is to come from last, but with only four runners the tactical space for a hold-up move is severely compressed and its STYLE_FIT flag tempers its prospects in a shape where natural position is unavailable.
runners_data.comment: Showmethebubbles has stayed competitive without threatening to win, finishing fifth in two of her last three starts, and she has already raced over today's distance. A 50-day layoff since her latest run is the concern, leaving fitness the obvious question against these on a modest rating of 58.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a four-runner field, this 6f nursery at Catterick is set up as a drifting, tactical affair where the early pace is likely to be modest and uncontested. Lady Dublin (style unknown, moderate form) and Mardy Bum are the most likely to push forward by default, though neither has a clear lead-horse profile, meaning the field could bunch and surge into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole. Showmethebubbles is a genuine hold-up type who has been mapped to midfield due to redistribution — there are more natural rear-runners in this field than the race shape can cleanly accommodate, and Mardy Bum is the most likely to drift closer to the pace than its hold-up tag suggests. The race shape modestly favours horses who can travel in a handy position through a slow-run opening half and sustain their effort through Catterick's stiff uphill finish, giving a slight edge to prominent or midfield-tracking profiles over pure closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Tempo Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field drifts through the first three furlongs at a conservative pace, triggering a compressed sprint home.
scenarios.body: Mardy Bum and Lady Dublin, tracking close to a slow gallop, will be best placed to kick off a modest early tempo and sustain their runs up the hill; Catterick's straight six rewards those who settle handy and quicken late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Dublin or Mardy Bum sets a more genuine pace from the front and steals a march on the field.
scenarios.body: A lone leader posting honest splits on Catterick's slight undulations could build an unassailable lead before the final furlong kicks in; the absence of any confirmed chaser means no horse is guaranteed to track and haul them back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely honest and the leaders tie themselves up, leaving a vacuum for horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Sunrise At Dawn has shown ability to close from behind but has posted modest figures on good ground, limiting confidence; Showmethebubbles, though a true hold-up type, faces the challenge of finding enough room in a small field to produce its best finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic No-Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If every runner idles in the early stages and the race degenerates into a ragged, uneven dash with no clear rhythm.
scenarios.body: In a field of four with no natural leader, a completely flat pace creates lottery-style outcomes where positional luck and a clean passage dictate the result; any runner could be favoured by a fortunate pitch, making form assessment unreliable.

watchPoints.text: Mardy Bum — on a quick seven-day turnaround and could be sharper than rivals; watch whether Mark Winn opts to push forward early in the absence of a natural leader, which could prove decisive on Catterick's unforgiving straight.

Lady Dublin — Ollie Pears has a cold 14-day record (0/4) and the horse's undefined running style means it could be caught in no-man's land if the pace is falsely slow; monitor early position from stalls.

Showmethebubbles — returning from 50 days off and a true hold-up type squeezed into a four-runner field where genuine cover is almost non-existent; if Cam Hardie cannot find a rhythm at the back, the horse may be caught flat-footed in a sprint finish.

Sunrise At Dawn — three runs and no placed effort on good ground; Tom Eaves will look to come late but the horse may need the race to be truly run to make any impact, which is unlikely given the absence of front-running types.

races.name: Le Veinard 2026. Racing And Info Handicap

runners_data.name: Aberama Gold
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran that David O'Meara typically targets in these sprint handicaps; goes well on good ground (1W3P from six similar-going runs) and travels best from off the pace in a true test — this moderate tempo may blunt his finishing kick.|

runners_data.name: Archduke Ferdinand
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer runner with a sharp record at 6f on good ground (1W2P from nine), but his natural instinct is to race further back than the map shows — placed in midfield only because the field is congested with hold-up types, which constrains his ability to deliver his trademark late effort.|

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old has consistent placed form over this course-and-distance profile (1W4P from ten similar runs) and Joanna Mason rides patiently; comfortable in a prominent role and has finished second twice in recent outings, suggesting she is ready to convert.|

runners_data.name: Two Commanders
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old sets the pace here and Connor Beasley was aboard when it won over 6f on soft recently; racing as the lone leader is slightly out of its normal prominent-tracking role (STYLE_FIT 0.90) but an uncontested lead minimises that concern — fitness after 11 days is fine.|

runners_data.name: Kody B
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's three-year-old ran creditably over 6f on good ground twice recently and Tom Eaves rides; wears a tongue-strap, is a natural hold-up type, and the moderate pace set by Two Commanders is the chief risk — needs more gallop than this field is likely to generate.|

runners_data.name: Awraad
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has been off 63 days, a fitness question that compounds the tactical problem; genuinely wants to race from the rear but is pushed into midfield here because of the hold-up congestion at the back — racing out of role (STYLE_FIT 0.91) and returning from a break.|

runners_data.name: Quercus
runners_data.note: Noel Wilson's nine-year-old has winning and placed form over 6f on good ground and wears a tongue-strap; a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to field congestion, which means it will struggle to execute its natural style and the moderate pace is unlikely to do it any favours either.|

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old has won three of its last six on good ground and David Allan takes the ride; wears a tongue-tie and is stepping up to 6f from recent 5f wins — the extra furlong is the key unknown, but prominent racing style and in-form profile make it one of the key players.|

races.paceDynamic: Two Commanders is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the outside, looks set to control proceedings at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 6f Catterick straight. Dream Deal and The Good Biscuit will track close from prominent positions, meaning the pace is unlikely to collapse but equally unlikely to be truly searching. This shape — a moderate, even tempo with a clear leader — historically favours horses that can race close to the pace and pounce entering the final furlong, rather than pure closers who need a strong early gallop to generate momentum. This field holds more hold-up horses than the race can accommodate at the back: Archduke Ferdinand, Awraad, and Quercus are all natural hold-up types who will find themselves competing for midfield berths rather than their preferred rear position, reducing their chance of delivering a true late sweep. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers and horses comfortable travelling in the first three or four are best suited, with deep closers likely to find this pace insufficient to carry them through from off the bridle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Two Commanders controls the gallop and Dream Deal or The Good Biscuit track closely enough to pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Two Commanders sets a measured pace that suits horses in the first two or three, and those prominent types get a perfect tow into the straight before asserting; the moderate tempo means closers simply cannot generate the momentum to reel them in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Bursts Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the hold-up horses find clear runs to deliver genuine late challenges.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace injection would shorten the winning time and open a gap for horses like Aberama Gold or Kody B to find their stride late; however this scenario requires the pace to be set more aggressively than Two Commanders' profile suggests.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dream Deal Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Deal is allowed to coast up alongside Two Commanders and the two share the lead, stretching the field.
scenarios.body: With Dream Deal's strong recent form over 5f and a preference for forcing tactics, a shared lead could see the pair quicken off it together in the final two furlongs; Dream Deal's hat-trick form on good ground makes it dangerous if allowed to dictate on its own terms.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of hold-up horses into midfield creates traffic and interference that lets one of them sneak through on the inside.
scenarios.body: Archduke Ferdinand, Awraad, and Quercus are all racing out of their natural role and could be shuffled further back still, but if gaps open along the rail one could steal a tactical advantage; this scenario is discounted precisely because none of these three are genuine hold-up horses executing their natural style.

watchPoints.text: Two Commanders and Dream Deal — if Dream Deal tracks the leader closely on the stand side, watch whether Two Commanders is pushed into a quicker gallop than it wants, which could unsettle the whole pace scenario.

Aberama Gold — Daniel Tudhope is an excellent judge of pace but this horse needs a stronger tempo to unleash its finishing kick; if the gallop is as moderate as expected, watch for Tudhope cutting his losses early rather than waiting for a run.

Awraad — 63 days off the track combined with racing out of its natural hold-up position makes this one to watch for signs of ring rustiness in the early stages; could compromise other runners if it gets unbalanced in the first furlong.

The Good Biscuit — Joanna Mason has placed this horse prominently with great consistency and it is the one most likely to be poised directly behind Two Commanders at halfway; watch its position at the 2f marker as a key indicator of where the race is won.
Quercus and Archduke Ferdinand — both natural hold-up horses competing for the same rear-to-midfield space; watch for them interfering with each other's run at a critical stage if a gap opens late.

races.name: Try Racing Tv For Free Now Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mudamer
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old prominent racer in form at this course and trip (placed three of last four at 7f, good-ish ground), though the race shape has pushed him into a hold-up slot he would never naturally occupy, which meaningfully blunts his chance if he cannot access his usual forward berth.
runners_data.comment: Mudamer has been consistent without adding a win, filling third spot twice in his last five starts and returning within four weeks of his latest run. He rates strongly on our figures at 87, well above his official mark of 81, and has already raced over today's distance, leaving turning those places into more as the target.

runners_data.name: Haaderr
runners_data.note: The key pace angle here — a confirmed front-runner who simply needs to step back up to race fitness after 281 days off; Edward Bethell's yard has been firing (11/32 in 14 days) and Daniel Tudhope commands this track, making the layoff the sole material risk.
runners_data.comment: Haaderr won his latest start after finishing runner-up in the two before, form that reads well, and he arrives with a trainer firing at 34% in the last fortnight having already raced over today's distance. The worry is fitness: a 281-day absence is a long time to be fresh.

runners_data.name: Naval Light
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old arrives here six weeks after his last run having won at 6f on soft and placed at 7f on good going — the combination of a close-tracking style and a 5lb claimer gives him a realistic route to winning if he can simply sit second and outstay Haaderr.
runners_data.comment: Naval Light won his latest start, bouncing back from a below-form eighth two starts back, having been third, third and second in the three runs before that, and tops our figures at 91. Already proven over today's distance, he rates the one to beat despite a 54-day gap since that win.

runners_data.name: Woodstock
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old carries visor headgear and is a genuine prominent type by nature, but the sheer volume of pace in this small field means she is almost certain to be pushed wider and further back than she wants — her recent form (three placed efforts at 7f on good) flatters a forward position she may not get.
runners_data.comment: Woodstock has stayed competitive without adding a win, a third-placed effort three starts back the highlight, and returns within a month of his latest run. He rates strongly on our figures at 86, well clear of his official mark of 74, and has already raced over today's distance.

races.paceDynamic: Haaderr is the confirmed front-runner and, in a field of just four, will dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop over Catterick's seven furlongs without any genuine pressure from behind. Naval Light is the one most likely to track closely in second, while Mudamer and Woodstock — both true prominent types — are displaced from their natural positions by the weight of pace in this small field, with Mudamer mapped to hold-up and Woodstock to midfield. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position; Haaderr and Naval Light are most likely to actually hold the prime early slots, leaving Woodstock and Mudamer unable to race where they want. A controlled, single-pace affair at 7f on good ground at Catterick will favour a horse capable of sustaining effort from a close-up position rather than one relying on a late burst from an unnatural hold-up berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Haaderr Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Haaderr goes unchallenged to the front and sets a measured, uncontested gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Haaderr controls every yard of the race, turning for home with a full tank and quickening clear before rivals can respond; a long layoff (281 days) is the only caveat, but the Bethell yard is in form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Naval Light Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Naval Light sits tight on Haaderr's heels, times the move perfectly and pounces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Having scored at 6f on soft and placed repeatedly at 7f on good, Naval Light possesses the tactical speed to exploit a prominent pitch; the 5lb claim from Nicholls helps offset the weight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, All Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or stalls and the field bunches, allowing backmarkers to get involved.
scenarios.body: Woodstock or Mudamer, forced wide of their natural roles, could pick up pieces if the tempo flatters late-movers; however, neither is a genuine hold-up type, reducing the authenticity of any late challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Haaderr Flops On Comeback
scenarios.trigger: If Haaderr's 281-day absence tells and he fades badly in the final two furlongs, scrambling the result.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine pace-setter the race loses shape entirely, handing an unexpected opportunity to Naval Light who can pivot to the front or Mudamer tracking closely; this remains a low-probability outcome given Bethell's strong recent 14-day strike rate.

watchPoints.text: Haaderr's 281-day layoff is the single biggest swing factor — if he is anything less than forward-fit he will capitulate in the final furlong and completely reshape the result.
Woodstock's visor headgear could sharpen early speed and create brief pressure on Haaderr into the first couple of furlongs, potentially forcing a faster early tempo than the map suggests.

Naval Light must be tracked through the early exchanges — if he is allowed to sit directly behind Haaderr and ration his effort, he becomes a serious threat in the final 1.5 furlongs at a generous weight.

Mudamer's redistribution to a hold-up role is artificial; watch to see if David Allan ignores the traffic and pushes forward — if he does, early crowding among three-wide prominent types could compromise the whole field's rhythm.

races.name: Racing Again 22nd July Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: South Shore
runners_data.note: Five-furlong specialist with back-to-back wins on good and standard going, ridden by Marco Ghiani and trained by Robert Cowell who is in strong form (1/8 over 14 days); prominent style suits this race shape perfectly and the 9-day turnaround is not a concern given the recent winning thread.
runners_data.comment: South Shore has won his last two starts, following a third before that, and returns quickly just nine days on. He tops our figures at 67 from stall four, already proven over today's distance, and looks fit to defy this on current form.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson sends this eight-year-old out just two days after its last run, which is an eyecatcher, but it has managed only one placing from five attempts on good ground at this trip and will be racing ahead of its natural prominent role by being cast as the sole leader here.
runners_data.comment: Our Absent Friends rates competitively on our figures at 67 from stall two, with a third three starts back the best of a lean recent sequence. He returns just two days after his last run, an unusually quick turnaround, though that latest effort itself was modest.

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's four-year-old owns the best recent form profile in this field — won and placed at five furlongs on good ground with James Sullivan up — and is the hold-up horse most likely to pose a genuine threat if a gap appears in the straight, though its deeper position in a crowded rear group is a practical obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Invincible Crown won last time out. He was runner-up two starts back, form that reads well on paper, and he has already raced over today's distance from stall six. Our figures rate him no higher than his official mark of 60 though, only seventh of nine in this field, leaving little apparent upside despite that recent upturn.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: A seasoned eight-year-old with three places at five furlongs on good ground and a hood fitted; David Allan rides, but its true nature as a deep hold-up horse is squeezed here — pushed into a midfield slot it would not naturally occupy, so its best tactical expression is compromised in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Albegone was runner-up last time out, his second such placing among his last six starts, and rates well on our figures at 63 from stall seven having already raced over today's distance. He returns within a month of that effort, with the lack of a win in that sequence the only knock against him.

runners_data.name: Edmond Halley
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's lightly-raced four-year-old returns after 81 days off — the longest absence in the field — with an explicit tendency to fade in the finish flagged, a deep draw on hold-up tactics, and no wins or places on good ground; this profile is the most vulnerable in a sustainable-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Edmond Halley's recent form reads modest, three unplaced efforts either side of a seventh and a fifth, and he has been off the track for 81 days. In his favour, he has already raced over today's distance and joins a yard firing at 34% over the last fortnight, which offers some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Lucius Aurelius
runners_data.note: Won at five furlongs on good ground and has placed four times from six, with a hood added; Kevin Ryan sends Jack Nicholls (5) in, and a 16-day return looks fresh enough, though the horse's hold-up style means it needs the pace to develop honestly before it can deliver.
runners_data.comment: Lucius Aurelius won four starts back but the form since has been mixed, rallying to third two starts back. A below-par eighth last time out followed, and he rates competitively at 64 from stall nine having already raced over today's distance. He returns 16 days on, leaving room for a bounce-back.

runners_data.name: Irish Dancer
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's six-year-old boasts two wins and five places from eight efforts on good ground, ridden by Zak Wheatley, with tongue tie and a bar operation listed — the prominent running style is a strong structural fit for this pace shape and recent course-distance-going form makes it one of the most relevant profiles here.
runners_data.comment: Irish Dancer won four starts back and has stayed competitive since, third last time out after a runner-up two back, though an eighth three starts back shows the odd blank. He rates a fair 62 from stall eight, has already raced over today's distance, and returns within three weeks of that latest run.

runners_data.name: Zuffolo
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's six-year-old carries a hood and a style-fit flag — its true identity as a hold-up type has been pushed into midfield on the map because the back of the field is already full; Rhys Elliott (5) rides, and while there is a placed effort on good ground, the horse is unlikely to secure the position where it would be most dangerous.
runners_data.comment: Zuffolo's recent form is modest, two eighths and two unplaced efforts in his last five starts, with only a second-placed run to suggest more. He rates down among the tail of this field at 58 from stall one, though he has raced over today's distance before and returns within a month of his last outing.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old is the youngest in the field and the lightest-weighted, with Connor Beasley aboard; placed on good ground earlier this season but its natural closing style is compressed into a midfield slot where it lacks the room to switch off properly, and limited good-ground exposure (2/5 by sample) adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Gwen Tennyson is rated bottom of this field on our figures at 48 from stall three, some way below her official mark of 53, despite a third-placed effort three starts back. She has already raced over today's distance and returns quickly, but little else in this form line inspires on our numbers.

races.paceDynamic: Our Absent Friends is the lone confirmed front-runner here, and with only one horse committed to leading, the tempo is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured — a relatively honest gallop on good turf over five furlongs at Catterick. South Shore and Irish Dancer are the genuine prominent types best placed to sit just off the leader and pounce before the turn into the short home straight, while the bulk of this field — Invincible Crown, Albegone, Lucius Aurelius, Edmond Halley, Zuffolo, and Gwen Tennyson — are natural hold-up horses who will be chasing from further back. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Albegone, Zuffolo, and Gwen Tennyson are true closers redistributed to midfield on the map because genuine late-run positions are already saturated, meaning they are unlikely to switch off as naturally as their profiles demand. This race shape strongly favours prominent-raced horses who can hold a position just behind a single, uncontested leader and unleash a finishing effort rounding the final bend — South Shore and Irish Dancer are structurally best placed, while genuine hold-up horses face an uphill task breaking from a traffic-heavy mid-pack with limited real estate to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Our Absent Friends sets a comfortable, uncontested lead and the race develops at a fair but unhurried pace, allowing South Shore and Irish Dancer to track into a winning position.
scenarios.body: Our Absent Friends controls the fractions unchallenged, and the two prominent holders draft into contention approaching the final furlong, benefiting from a clean run and the short Catterick straight favouring those who arrive with momentum already building.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently to string the field and leave the closer enough daylight in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Invincible Crown, who has won and placed repeatedly at five furlongs on good ground, is best credentialled of the genuine hold-up horses and could exploit a gap if the prominent pair burn each other slightly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Our Absent Friends dictates a truly dawdling tempo and is never challenged, effectively turning it into a sprint from a standing start.
scenarios.body: Running entirely out of role for a horse whose profile demands being ridden prominently rather than truly leading, Our Absent Friends could steal enough of an advantage that none of the hold-up pack can close in time — though its 2-day turnaround and modest good-ground figures make this fragile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up cluster causes interference mid-pack and one of the redistributed types finds a gap late against the inside rail.
scenarios.body: Zuffolo or Gwen Tennyson, though racing out of their natural deep-closer role and with reduced style-fit probability, could capitalise on a messy finish if the prominent horses block each other — a low-probability but non-zero scenario given the density of horses in the middle ground.

watchPoints.text: Our Absent Friends runs just two days after its last outing — monitor market confidence at the off; if it shows any signs of fatigue mid-race it could capitulate quickly and leave the field shape-less.

The cluster of Albegone, Zuffolo, and Gwen Tennyson, all natural hold-up types crammed into midfield, creates a genuine interference risk in the first two furlongs as they compete for the same ground — back-end runners should be tracked for early traffic trouble.

Edmond Halley's 81-day absence combined with a tendency to fade in the finish makes it an active danger to the horses around it rather than a winning threat — riders tracking it should be alert to it weakening sharply inside the final furlong.

South Shore's jockey Marco Ghiani and trainer Robert Cowell are in a 1/8 strike rate over 14 days — stable form is live and worth noting against a horse whose recent back-to-back wins on similar ground underpin its profile here.

Irish Dancer's tongue tie and bar operation headgear combination is worth monitoring for any pre-race behavioural signs; the horse has strong going-specific form but a first-time or returned piece of headgear can introduce unpredictability in the stalls.
